questions.question: If your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery, when should you turn off the engine?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before unhooking the hoses.
questions.explanation: If your engine runs a pump for product transfer, turn it off after the transfer is complete. But turn it off before you unhook the hoses.

questions.question: ____ are most affected by strong winds.
questions.correctAnswerText: Light vehicles
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. Light commercial vehicles are especially affected by strong winds.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and others while driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Important.
questions.explanation: You must maintain safe space between your vehicle and others. This space allows you to stop safely without hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: To prevent rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside a trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
questions.explanation: Cargo placed high in a trailer makes the vehicle top-heavy and more likely to roll over. Place cargo as low as possible to reduce this risk.

questions.question: How should hazardous and non-hazardous materials be distinguished on a shipping paper?

options.text: List hazardous materials at the bottom of the paper.
List hazardous materials at the top of the paper.
Highlight hazardous materials in the same color as non-hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: List hazardous materials at the top of the paper.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must be clearly separated from non-hazardous materials. You can do this by listing them first, highlighting them in a different color, or marking them with an "X" in a column labeled "HM."

questions.question: During inspection, what is most important to check on a tank vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks.
questions.explanation: Check for leaks first. Transporting gas or liquid in a leaking tank is illegal and unsafe.

questions.question: When loading liquid cargo, you should consider the ____ .
questions.correctAnswerText: Weight of the liquid
questions.explanation: Consider how much the liquid will expand during transport, the weight of the liquid, and legal weight limits when loading.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color identifies service lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Air lines are color-coded to prevent mistakes when connecting hoses. Blue identifies service lines. Red identifies emergency lines.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Rims with a missing lug nut are acceptable if four other lug nuts remain.
A cracked lock ring is acceptable at speeds under 55 mph.
A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
Welded repairs are acceptable for rear axle wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lug nuts are dangerous defects. Do not use cracked or bent lock rings. Wheels or rims with welded repairs are not safe.

questions.question: A commercial vehicle should:

options.text: Have a fire extinguisher only if transporting hazardous materials.
Have a fire extinguisher only when traveling through remote areas.
Always have at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always have at least one fire extinguisher.
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes at least one fire extinguisher, spare fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for when parked.

questions.question: If you are backing up and become unsure about your path, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and get out to look.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to look.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure of your path while backing, you should stop the vehicle, get out, and check your path of travel.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after driving a short distance to:

options.text: Recheck the tightness of the lug nuts.
See if rocks are in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Recheck the tightness of the lug nuts.
questions.explanation: After driving a short distance with a new tire, stop and check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: Older trailers without spring brakes will lose their brakes if:

options.text: The trailer will not have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will not have brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers without spring brakes have no brakes if the air supply leaks. The wheels will spin freely with no braking power.

questions.question: Large combination vehicles take the longest time to stop when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Empty.
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. Without weight, the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: If you must back up, it is helpful to:

options.text: Back up as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Walk your path first to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk your path first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, exit the vehicle and walk your path to look for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both side mirrors.

questions.question: Slippery roads usually:

options.text: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to drive a vehicle.
Can be avoided by driving at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Drive carefully when road conditions are slippery.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a minor truck fire, you should:

options.text: Check if the doors are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: Feel the doors first to see if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a fire inside the cargo. If so, keep the doors closed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume other drivers don't see you. Be ready for them to move into your path. You may tap your horn lightly or flash your lights as you pass.

questions.question: When driving a tank truck, a surge:

options.text: Is not a concern for drivers.
Does not usually happen with liquids.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Partially-filled liquid tanks can surge. Surge happens when liquid waves from one side of the tank to another, making the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: Escape ramps are:

options.text: Ramps to exit the interstate quickly.
Ramps connecting four-lane and two-lane highways.
Ramps used to stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.
Ramps that cannot be used by automobiles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ramps used to stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep hills to safely stop runaway vehicles. They have loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.
